summary_line: The Self is unsupported, all-supporting, desireless, and eternally unchanging.

translations.author: English Translation
translations.text: I am without any support, and I am the support of all. I am of the nature of one whose desires are fully fulfilled. I am indeed the Self, indestructible and changeless.

summary_line: The Self is eternally free, distinct from all bodies and states, and is the unchanging witness.

translations.author: English Translation
translations.text: I am free from the threefold afflictions—those arising from the body, from other beings, and from divine forces. I am distinct from the gross, subtle, and causal bodies. I am the witness of the three states of waking, dreaming, and deep sleep. I am indeed the Self, imperishable and unchanging.

translations.author: Hindi Translation
translations.text: मैं त्रिविध तापों—शरीर से, अन्य प्राणियों से और दिव्य शक्तियों से उत्पन्न होने वाले—से मुक्त हूँ। मैं स्थूल, सूक्ष्म और कारण शरीरों से भिन्न हूँ। मैं जाग्रत, स्वप्न और सुषुप्ति अवस्थाओं का साक्षी हूँ। मैं निश्चय ही अक्षय और अपरिवर्तनशील आत्मा हूँ।

word_by_word.word_english:
Free from the threefold afflictions
त्रिविध तापों से मुक्त

Distinct from the three bodies
स्थूल, सूक्ष्म और कारण शरीरों से भिन्न

मैं जाग्रत, स्वप्न और सुषुप्ति अवस्थाओं का साक्षी हूँ

I am indeed the Self, imperishable
मैं निश्चय ही आत्मा हूँ, अक्षय

summary_line: The seer (Brahman) and the seen (Maya) are eternally distinct — the core of Vedanta’s non-dual teaching.
